correctness.rationale: An odd-order abelian group table has no intercalate: the Latin 2x2 equations imply 2(c1-c2)=0 and hence c1=c2. The inspected Cioabă–Mim field-homology theorem therefore gives reduced homology only H2 with dimension (n-1)^3. Every nontrivial translation acts freely on cells with odd orbit length>=3; a setwise invariant clique contains such an orbit, forcing u=0 or v=0 or u+v=0, exactly one axis. An outside cell meets a preserved row/column/sum line in at most two positions, so every preserved clique lies wholly on one of n disjoint lines. A preserved full simplex has alternating oriented-face trace 1, hence Lefschetz L(t)=n on axes and 0 elsewhere, with H0 trace 1; at identity H2 dimension known. The resulting character is product of three augmentation characters and gives a rational isomorphism by characteristic-zero semisimplicity, with Fourier multiplicity n-|{1,alpha,beta}|. Independent exact n=5 clique enumeration yielded 515 nonempty faces, and representative translation characters (identity64, axes4, off-axes -1) matched formula.
residual_risks: The homology concentration relies on cited published Latin-square theorem; independent n=5 finite trace checks cannot certify all groups.
